questions.q: You ___ wear a seatbelt — it's the law.
I ___ go to the dentist — my tooth hurts.
You ___ eat so much sugar — it's bad for you.

questions.explanation: 'Don't have to' means it's not necessary (no obligation).
questions.q: You ___ bring anything — just come!
Students ___ do their homework.
You look tired — you ___ rest.

options: You must to wear a uniform.
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
You ___ park here — it's forbidden.

questions.explanation: 'Had to' is the past form of 'must'/'have to'.
questions.q: She ___ work late yesterday — the boss asked her.
You ___ see a doctor about that cough.
We ___ hurry — we have plenty of time.
You ___ smoke in here — it's against the rules.
I ___ wear glasses — I can't see well.
It's raining — you ___ take an umbrella.

questions.explanation: 'Must' takes the infinitive without 'to': 'must be', not 'must to be'.
questions.q: Which sentence is WRONG?
Do I ___ pay now, or later?
You ___ eat with your mouth open — it's rude.
Passengers ___ turn off their phones.

questions.explanation: 'Has to' + infinitive: third person -s on 'has', not on the verb.
questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
You ___ tell anyone — it's a secret!
